summary:
We built "AEGIS", an on-board mental health and team cohesion platform designed to keep astronauts connected, supported, and working smoothly together on deep-space missions.
Living in tight quarters millions of miles from Earth puts immense pressure on a crew, especially when communication delays make real-time support from home impossible. To tackle this, AEGIS combines daily health and stress tracking—like sleep quality, workload, and subtle shifts in vocal or text tone—with a built-in "AI Psychologist". Grounded in real psychological practices like Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), the AI Psychologist acts as a supportive, private sounding board. It spots early signs of burnout or crew tension and helps astronauts talk things through before small frustrations turn into major conflicts. At the same time, it securely packages key mental health trends to send back to flight surgeons on Earth, while keeping personal conversations strictly private on the ship.
On long journeys to the Moon or Mars, a crew's teamwork is just as vital as their spacecraft. AEGIS helps astronauts stay resilient and united when Earth is out of reach—and brings accessible mental health tools to isolated teams right here at home.
details:
Our project is an autonomous, proactive AI Psychological Support System designed specifically for astronauts on deep-space missions (such as lunar or Mars expeditions), where up to a 20-minute communication delay makes real-time therapy from Mission Control impossible.

Unlike traditional chatbots that wait for a user to report a problem, our AI operates passively in the background using multimodal biometric and behavioral indicators, including simulated heart rate variability, sleep cycles, and voice stress patterns. When it detects early signs of hidden burnout, sensory monotony, or acute stress, it gently initiates a voice-first, zero-friction check-in. Powered by a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture grounded in official NASA Behavioral Health and Performance protocols and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy frameworks, the AI delivers accurate, clinically sound guidance without relying on generic responses.

What makes our solution truly creative is how it solves specific psychological challenges of spaceflight. First, its proactive biometric triggers identify silent fatigue before an astronaut is even aware of it, bypassing the common tendency of flight crews to underreport psychological distress. Second, the "Earth Anchor" Memory Capsule counteracts the Earth-Out-of-View Phenomenon and sensory deprivation by unlocking personalized, pre-recorded audio and video messages from loved ones precisely when emotional resilience dips. Third, a built-in Crew Empathy Buffer acts as a real-time communication assistant that detects sharp tones in team messages, suggesting neutral rephrasings to prevent micro-conflicts in confined habitats. All of this is wrapped in a glanceable, zero-friction UI featuring a calm ambient voice interface and a minimalist visual wave indicator designed for overloaded schedules.

The primary benefit of our project is 100% onboard autonomy and strict privacy—all psychological data stays locally on the spacecraft, giving crew members a safe space to seek support without fear of being grounded from mission tasks. In the long term, this technology protects crew cohesion, prevents mission-critical human errors caused by mental fatigue, and establishes a scalable mental health standard for deep-space exploration as well as isolated environments on Earth, such as polar research stations and submarines.

To develop this project, our team combined multiple AI models—integrating Large Language Models with a custom knowledge base of space psychology guidelines alongside sentiment and voice-stress analysis—with modern prototyping and web development tools, utilizing open NASA behavioral health research data. Throughout the process, we carefully considered key human factors including communication latency, astronaut privacy, low cognitive load through voice-first interaction, and calming dark-mode aesthetics to reduce visual overstimulation inside spacecraft modules.
